title: Block: Sliding Window With a Hashmap
oneLiner: Find the longest substring with at most k distinct characters, growing a window on the right and shrinking it on the left.
keyTakeaway: Grow right every step; shrink left only while the window is invalid; measure after shrinking. Delete a key when its count drops to 0, or the map's size lies.
explanation:
Return the length of the longest substring of s that contains at most k distinct characters. "eceba" with k = 2 gives 3 ("ece").

Keep counts of the characters inside the window s[left..right]. Each step adds s[right]. While the map holds more than k keys, remove s[left]: decrease its count, delete it at 0, and move left on. After the while loop the window is valid, so right - left + 1 is a candidate. Longest Substring Without Repeats, Fruit Into Baskets and Character Replacement are this block with a different validity test.

gotchas: Off-by-one on the window: its length is right - left + 1.
Not deleting a key when its count reaches 0, so the map counts characters that left the window.
Measuring the window before shrinking it, while it is still invalid.

complexity.note: right and left each move across the string once, so the work is O(n); the map holds at most k + 1 characters.
